message.content:
FADE IN:

EXT. LAKESIDE DOCK — LATE AFTERNOON

The sky is a bruise of amber and violet. The sun is halved — a thin crescent of light bleeding through the corona. The air hums.

A WOODEN BOAT sits in the still water. A FARMHAND, calloused, weathered, stands at the edge of the dock. His hands are stained with the day's work.

The LINE snaps. A WIDE SILVER FISH thrashes on the hook, gasping. The FARMHAND tugs the line — the fish leaps clear of the water, belly-up, gills flapping, water beading off its scales.

FARMHAND (O.S.): "Hold steady, little silverback."

The fish is lifted to a level where it stares at the eclipsed sky. Its eyes catch the corona. The fish, in its silvered belly, sees the dark ring of the Moon's edge. The fish's eyes do not blink.

The FARMHAND murmurs: "There. You are not lost. You are only... on the other side of the day."

The fish's mouth opens, a slow silver pucker. Its eyes catch the corona. The water, far below, still.

The FARMHAND lowers the fish back to the water. The line slackens. The fish dives.

CUT TO: THE SKY

The corona is a full ring of fire. The eclipse is the first the FARMHAND has seen. He tilts his head.

The fish is gone. The water is a dark, mirror of the eclipsed sky.

---
